metadata.title: A Multimodal Approach To Detect User’s Emotion

abstract: The paper presents a multimodal approach to detect user emotions by analyzing keystroke dynamics, text semantics, and heart rate variations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating these elements for emotion detection.

research.problem: Detecting user emotions using multimodal data (keystroke dynamics, text analysis, and heart rate variation).
research.motivation: Enhance systems like perceptual computing by enabling machines to adapt to user emotional states.
research.objective: Propose a multimodal framework for emotion recognition through text, keystroke patterns, and physiological signals.

methodology.summary: Combines keystroke dynamics, text analysis (JAWS/NLTK), and heart rate variation (PPG) for emotion detection.

experiments.experimental_setup: Used webcam for PPG signal extraction, JAWS/NLTK for text analysis, and standardized datasets for emotion classification.
experiments.results: NLTK approach outperformed JAWS in emotion intensity detection. Heart rate variation correlated with emotional states.

contributions: First multimodal integration of keystroke dynamics, text semantics, and heart rate for emotion detection
analysis.research_gap: Complexity of human emotions requires more nuanced classification frameworks.

sections.introduction: Emotions influence behavior and require machine adaptation. The paper proposes a multimodal system to detect user emotions through text, keystroke patterns, and physiological signals.
sections.related_work: Existing work focuses on text-based emotion detection. This paper introduces a multimodal approach combining keystroke dynamics and physiological signals.
sections.methodology: Keystroke dynamics (session time, latency), text analysis (JAWS/NLTK), and heart rate variation (PPG) are integrated for emotion detection.
sections.results: NLTK outperformed JAWS in text analysis. Heart rate variation correlated with emotional states across datasets.
sections.discussion: Multimodal integration improves detection accuracy. Challenges include physiological signal noise and text ambiguity.
sections.conclusion: The proposed system demonstrates effective emotion detection through multimodal analysis, with potential applications in adaptive computing systems.

metadata.title: Recognising Emotions from Keyboard Stroke Pattern

abstract: The paper explores recognizing emotional states (neutral, positive, negative) from keyboard stroke patterns using classifiers like Simple Logistics, SMO, and Multilayer Perceptron. It emphasizes the role of emotions in human-computer interaction and validates results through empirical studies with 300 participants.

research.problem: Recognizing emotional states from keyboard interaction patterns.
research.motivation: Enhance human-computer interaction by understanding user emotions through non-verbal behavioral cues.
research.objective: Analyze keyboard stroke data to classify emotional states and evaluate classifier performance.
research_questions: How do emotional states affect typing patterns?
Which classifiers best predict emotional categories from keyboard data?

methodology.summary: Used WEKA classifiers to analyze features extracted from keyboard stroke data, correlating typing patterns with self-reported emotional states.
datasets: 300 participants' typing data (41 used in experiments)
preprocessing: Mapped emotional states to typing patterns
methodology.training_strategy: Used WEKA for feature analysis and classifier evaluation.
evaluation_metrics: Recognition rates for negative/positive vs neutral states

experiments.experimental_setup: 300 participants (45% female, 55% male) typed predefined paragraphs while reporting emotional states. 41 users provided typed data for analysis.
experiments.results: BF Tree achieved 89.02% recognition for negative vs neutral, J48 88.88% for positive vs neutral. Negative states showed clearer typing pattern differences.

contributions: Demonstrated keyboard stroke patterns as a viable modality for emotion recognition
Validated classifier effectiveness for emotional state classification
limitations: Self-reported emotional states may introduce bias
future_work: Integrate Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM) for emotion measurement
analysis.research_gap: Need for robust methods to handle inconsistent data and cross-modal emotion recognition

sections.introduction: Highlights the importance of emotions in decision-making and interaction, proposing keyboard stroke analysis as a novel approach for emotion recognition.
sections.related_work: Reviews studies on facial expressions, audio, and gesture-based emotion recognition, noting limited research on keyboard modalities.
sections.methodology: Describes data collection from participants typing predefined texts and feature extraction using WEKA classifiers.
sections.results: Presents classification accuracy rates for negative/positive vs neutral states across six algorithms.
sections.discussion: Analyzes how emotional states influence typing patterns (e.g., reduced speed for negative states, increased speed for positive states).
sections.conclusion: Summarizes keyboard stroke patterns as a feasible method for emotion recognition, emphasizing the need for larger datasets and multimodal approaches.

metadata.title: Does Keystroke Dynamics tell us about Emotions? A Systematic Literature Review and Dataset Construction

abstract: The paper investigates how keystroke dynamics can be used for emotion recognition through a systematic literature review. It highlights the effectiveness of keystroke biometrics in identifying emotional states, summarizes data acquisition methods, features, classification techniques, and performance metrics. The authors construct a new dataset via an interactive web application to address the scarcity of emotion recognition datasets in this domain.

research.problem: Understanding human emotions in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) to improve system performance and decision-making.
research.motivation: Emotional states significantly impact human behavior and interactions, necessitating robust emotion recognition methods for intelligent systems.
research.objective: Systematically evaluate keystroke dynamics for emotion recognition and construct a new dataset to advance research in this area.
research_questions: What are the trends in online emotion recognition technologies?
Keystroke dynamics in emotion recognition: applications, strengths, and weaknesses?
What features are extracted from typing rhythms?
Which classification techniques are used for emotion recognition?
What evaluation measures and performance metrics are employed?
What existing datasets are available for emotion recognition through keystroke dynamics?

methodology.summary: A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted following Kitchenham and Charters' guidelines, with defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and search strategies.
datasets: Constructed dataset via interactive web application

experiments.results: Best accuracy rates achieved: 91.24% for 'fright' emotion using SVM, 84% for arousal, and 83% for valence using KNN.

contributions: Systematic review of keystroke dynamics for emotion recognition
Construction of a new dataset via web application
future_work: Develop automatic emotion recognition systems based on keystroke dynamics
analysis.research_gap: Scarcity of datasets specifically focused on emotion recognition through keystroke dynamics

sections.introduction: Emotion is a fundamental aspect of human behavior, and its recognition is critical for intelligent systems. Keystroke dynamics offer a non-intrusive method for emotion detection, motivating this study.
sections.related_work: Previous studies focus on physiological states, facial expressions, speech, and text for emotion recognition, but keystroke dynamics remain underexplored.
sections.methodology: A systematic literature review was conducted using SCOPUS, with defined search terms and inclusion/exclusion criteria to analyze existing research.
sections.results: The review identified trends in emotion recognition technologies, strengths/weaknesses of keystroke dynamics, extracted features, classification methods, and evaluation metrics.
sections.discussion: Keystroke dynamics provide cost-effective, real-time emotion recognition but face challenges like data volume and external interference. The constructed dataset addresses existing gaps.
sections.conclusion: This work highlights the potential of keystroke dynamics for emotion recognition and proposes a new dataset to advance future research in this area.

metadata.title: Evaluating Effectiveness of Smartphone Typing as an Indicator of User Emotion
metadata.venue: 7th International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction (ACII)

abstract: The paper explores smartphone typing as a modality for detecting multiple affective states (happy, sad, stressed, relaxed). An Android-based system called TapSense is developed to analyze typing features like speed, backspaces, and special characters. Results show 73% average accuracy (AUCROC) using typing features alone, with typing speed being the most discriminative feature.

research.problem: Detecting user emotions using smartphone typing patterns as a non-intrusive, low-overhead modality.
research.motivation: Keystroke dynamics on desktops are effective for emotion detection; smartphone typing offers similar potential with better in-situ experiment coverage.
research.objective: Evaluate smartphone typing features for multi-state emotion detection and develop a system with high accuracy.
research_questions: Can smartphone typing features effectively detect multiple emotion states?
Which typing features are most discriminative for emotion classification?

methodology.summary: TapSense, an Android-based system, collects typing features (speed, backspaces, special characters) and self-reported emotions via Experience Sampling Method (ESM). Data is balanced using SMOTE for classification.
preprocessing: Data cleaning to remove No Response and outlier sessions
methodology.training_strategy: Personalized machine learning models trained on typing features and self-reported emotion labels.

experiments.experimental_setup: 3-week in-the-wild study with 22 participants using TapSense to collect typing data and self-reports.
baselines: Aggregate Model (AG, assuming similar typing patterns)
experiments.results: TapSense achieved 73% average accuracy (AUCROC) with maximum 94% for individual states. Typing speed was most discriminative.

contributions: Development of TapSense for emotion detection via smartphone typing
Identification of typing speed as key discriminative feature
analysis.research_gap: Limited studies on non-intrusive, context-agnostic emotion detection using smartphone typing.

sections.introduction: Focuses on leveraging smartphone typing patterns for emotion detection, building on desktop keystroke dynamics research.
sections.related_work: Covers existing touch-based emotion detection methods, including application-specific analysis and sensor-based approaches.
sections.methodology: Details TapSense architecture, ESM data collection, and feature extraction processes.
sections.results: Presents accuracy metrics, feature importance, and data balancing techniques.
sections.discussion: Analyzes the effectiveness of typing features and limitations of self-reported data.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes contributions and potential applications in affective computing.

metadata.title: Keystroke/Mouse Usage Based Emotion Detection and User Identification
authors: A. B. M. Alim Al Islam

abstract: The paper proposes a simplified emotion detection method using keystroke and mouse usage data, comparing classifiers like KNN and Bounded K-means Clustering. It also analyzes user identification challenges under emotional state influences.

research.problem: Traditional emotion detection requires significant infrastructure, necessitating a simpler, cost-effective approach.
research.motivation: To address the limitations of existing emotion detection systems and explore user identification through behavioral data.
research.objective: Develop a lightweight classifier for emotion detection and analyze user identification accuracy under emotional states.
research_questions: Can emotions be detected from keystroke/mouse data?
How effective is user identification under emotional state influences?

methodology.summary: Multimedia components induce emotional states, while keystroke/mouse data is collected via a custom survey. Classifiers like KNN and Bounded K-means Clustering analyze the data.
preprocessing: Data collection via multimedia-induced emotional states
methodology.training_strategy: Comparison of existing classifiers and newly proposed lightweight classifier

experiments.experimental_setup: 35 participants interacted with a survey system using multimedia clips to induce emotions, with keystroke/mouse data collected.
experiments.results: Bounded K-means Clustering achieved best performance for five emotional states. User identification accuracy declined under emotional state influences.

contributions: Survey system for emotion-induced data collection
Analysis of user identification under emotional states
limitations: Accuracy drops when emotional states blend in user identification
future_work: Testing with diverse emotional state combinations
analysis.research_gap: Limited exploration of blended emotional states' impact on user identification

sections.introduction: Introduces emotionally-aware systems and the need for cost-effective emotion detection methods.
sections.related_work: Reviews existing emotion detection approaches and user identification techniques.
sections.methodology: Details multimedia-based emotion induction and classifier-based data analysis.
sections.results: Presents classifier performance and user identification accuracy findings.
sections.discussion: Analyzes contributions, limitations, and future research directions.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes the effectiveness of keystroke/mouse data for emotion detection and user identification challenges.
